If such particles have a small mass, they are usually described as a purely classical field. However, it was recently shown that this description is incomplete: their inherent gravitational self-interactions can squeeze the field, producing a quantum feature beyond the classical description. Here we analyze squeezing of light dark matter in the presence of decoherence. We show that squeezing is continuously generated, and rapidly enough to survive dissipation, and may also remain present under thermal fluctuations and dephasing. Our results demonstrate that dark matter might possess persistent quantum features and motivate further investigation of their implications for dark matter detection.

hep-th.title: Gravitational Instability of Cold Axion Dark Matter Beyond Minimal Coupling
hep-th.author: Bryan Cordero-Patino, Álvaro Duenas-Vidal, Jorge Segovia
hep-th.abstract: Following recent observations of unexpectedly massive galaxies at high redshift by the James Webb Space Telescope, the revision of Dark Matter (DM) models --specifically regarding how DM couples to gravity-- has become a central topic in Cosmology. In this paper, we develop an axion model for Cold Dark Matter (CDM) with a non-minimal coupling to gravity. From this framework, we evaluate the gravitational instability in the hydrodynamic limit. Our results demonstrate how gravitational instabilities depend on the non-minimal coupling parameter, providing a novel tool for aligning with the high-redshift observations from the James Webb Space Telescope.

hep-th.title: Interferometric trilemma for ultraviolet-softened gravity
hep-th.author: Hiroki Matsui
hep-th.abstract: Ultraviolet-softened extensions of general relativity can weaken gravity at short distances, whereas a positive Källén--Lehmann spectral density forbids gravity from falling below Newtonian strength. Which property of the mediator must such a weakening sacrifice? For Lorentz-invariant Gaussian mediators coupled linearly to the conserved stress tensor, we formulate three independent interferometric conditions that jointly imply this bound: visibility is never amplified, decoherence is fixed by the energy radiated by the difference source, and no interferometer responds to a later one. At tree level, the three ghost prescriptions of quadratic gravity each violate exactly one: negative-norm ghosts amplify coherence, negative-energy ghosts decohere without positive energy transfer from the difference source, and a time-symmetric fakeon response produces advanced fringe shifts. Any universal short-distance weakening of gravity therefore certifies that its mediator violates one of these conditions, and the observables proposed to certify quantum gravity become consistency tests of its ultraviolet completion.

hep-th.title: The Geometry of the "Gauge Argument"
hep-th.author: James Owen Weatherall, Benjamin H. Feintzeig
hep-th.abstract: We show how the "gauge argument", widely criticized by philosophers as ad hoc and unconvincing, may be reconstructed rigorously, and, we believe, convincingly, as an argument concerning the geometry of vector bundles. In this form, the gauge argument has two parts, the first of which is strongly analogous to the Weyl-Stein argument for Galilean spacetime as the appropriate setting for Newtonian gravitation; and the second of which invokes a classic result in the Yang-Mills theory literature, due to Utiyama [1956, "Invariant Theoretical Interpretation of Interaction", Phys. Rev. 101, 1597].

hep-th.title: Black hole free energy landscapes from constrained instantons
hep-th.author: Shan-Ping Wu, Jia-Zhou Liu, Yu-Xiao Liu, Shao-Wen Wei
hep-th.abstract: We apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. Boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-Neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. Independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with Lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. For selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $I_{\rm constr}=\beta\mathcal F_{\rm gen}=\beta(E_{\mathcal B}-\Omega_{\mathcal B}^{I}J_{\mathcal B,I})-S$, with $\beta=T^{-1}$. Here $E_{\mathcal B}$ and $J_{\mathcal B,I}$ are renormalized Hamiltonian charges and $S$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. Interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. We extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{Riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. The same thermodynamic form follows with Wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes illustrate the Einstein construction, while five-dimensional static AdS black holes in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and the rotating BTZ branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.

hep-th.title: Construction of Causal Set Propagators in $2+1$-Dimensional Constant-Curvature Spacetimes from Two-Link Paths
hep-th.author: Arsim Kastrati
hep-th.abstract: We study a link-based retarded scalar propagator on causal sets sprinkled into $2+1$-dimensional Minkowski, anti-de Sitter, and de Sitter spacetimes. The construction is based on the squared link matrix $\mathbf{L}^2$, whose expectation value counts two-link paths between fixed endpoints. In the high-density limit, the dominant contribution localizes near the intersection of the null boundaries of the Alexandrov interval, and the flat-space normalization remains unchanged in constant curvature. The resulting kernels agree with the corresponding continuum Klein-Gordon propagators for a nominally massless scalar with effective curvature coupling $\xi_{\rm link}=1/6$. Since the conformal coupling in $2+1$ spacetime dimensions is $1/8$, this value is not a conformal-coupling effect. Together with link-based results in $1+1$ and $3+1$ dimensions, where the same coefficient $1/6$ appears, this suggests that the coupling may reflect an ultraviolet property of the link structure, reminiscent of the combination $(1/6-\xi)\mathcal{R}$ in local heat-kernel expansions.

hep-th.title: Geodesics of the five-dimensional Kerr-(A)dS black hole in closed form
hep-th.author: Özgür Sarıoğlu, Enes Yılmaz
hep-th.abstract: The Hamilton-Jacobi equation for geodesic motion in the five-dimensional Kerr-(A)dS black hole separates in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates, but the resulting first-order system has so far been integrated case by case, according to the real roots of the radial and the polar polynomial. We give the general solution in closed form. In dimensionless variables both polynomials are quartic, and a theorem of Biermann and Weierstrass then yields the radial and the polar coordinate as one pair of manifestly real formulas, parametrized by an arbitrary point of the orbit rather than by a turning point, and valid for timelike and null geodesics alike whatever the root structure. The time coordinate and the two azimuthal angles follow by quadratures that reduce to elliptic integrals of the third kind alone, and the affine parameter by one more of the same type. Along the way we correct the inverse metric and the radial potential as published.

hep-th.title: The NLL/NLO$^+$ QCD spectrum from Higgs-plus-charm correlations at the LHC
hep-th.author: Francesco Giovanni Celiberto, Francesca Lonigro
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the high-energy behavior of observables sensitive to the production of a Higgs boson in association with a singly charmed hadron at the $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV LHC, with light-flavored hadrons considered for comparison. Our reference formalism is the hybrid factorization at NLL/NLO$^+$, where the standard collinear picture is enhanced by the resummation of energy logarithms at the next-to-leading level and beyond. We present a prime phenomenological application of the next-to-leading correction to the singly off-shell Higgs emission function, as implemented in the multimodular JETHAD interface, a core element to test the stability of our high-energy distributions under energy-scale variations and to assess the weight of missing higher-order uncertainties. The resulting natural stability traces our path towards precision studies of Higgs production within high-energy next-to-leading-order QCD.

hep-th.title: Local Measurement Theory for Quantum Cellular Automata
hep-th.author: Tommaso Brambilla, Alessandro Tosini, Paolo Perinotti
hep-th.abstract: The formulation of quantum measurements compatible with relativistic causality is obstructed by the tension between the locality of observable algebras and the dynamical state transformations induced by measurement processes. We develop a local measurement theory for quantum cellular automata, lattices of finite-dimensional quantum systems with a causal reversible dynamics evolving in discrete time steps. Measurement processes are described by localized completely positive maps and organized into operational measurement protocols, finite non-adaptive sequences of local instruments distributed across the causal cone induced by the automaton local dynamics. Each protocol induces an effective measurement on the initial time slice, whose support is constrained by the causal structure generated by the automaton. Non-local measurement effects therefore arise through causal propagation and composition of local operations, rather than from primitive non-local interventions or instantaneous collapse prescriptions. We establish the corresponding spatial support bounds and characterize the resulting measurement architecture. As an explicit example, we construct a two-step protocol for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour qubit automaton which, for suitable automaton parameters, realizes a Bell-basis projective measurement on two neighbouring sites after coarse-graining of the local outcomes. Away from this point, the same protocol generates a continuous family of deformed Bell measurements whose entanglement and stabilizer Rényi non-classicality can be quantified explicitly. The framework thus provides a causally consistent operator-algebraic mechanism for synthesizing spatially extended quantum measurements from strictly local operations.

hep-th.title: Cosmological perturbations from localized sources: a gauge-invariant multipolar theory
hep-th.author: Geoffrey Compère, Sk Jahanur Hoque
hep-th.abstract: We develop a first-principles description of the linearized gravitational field of localized sources in spatially flat Friedmann-Lema\^ıtre-Robertson-Walker universes with arbitrary smooth expansion histories. The construction determines the complete retarded metric and the induced perturbation of the surrounding cosmic fluid from prescribed source stresses and a cosmologically stationary past field. It includes all multipole orders and accounts for curvature tails, through which the field depends on the source's past history inside the light cone. Generalizing the Blanchet-Damour multipolar formalism, we identify gauge-invariant mass and current moments together with a canonical cosmic fluid moment that determines an independent scalar response. This response vanishes in Minkowski and pure de Sitter spacetime, although curvature tails persist in de Sitter. The gauge-invariant multipoles are obtained directly in position space. This gives an exterior description without the nonlocal spatial projection through the source interior required by the usual scalar-vector-tensor decomposition. We also relate the canonical multipole metric to the standard variables of cosmological perturbation theory. The retarded construction requires neither a slow-motion nor a geometric-optics approximation. We define effective multipolar sources by truncating the moments of slowly varying sub-Hubble extended sources at a prescribed Cartesian multipole order, recovering the earlier quadrupolar and octupolar models in de Sitter spacetime. We recover the known Minkowski and de Sitter multipolar fields and obtain an analytical representation for gravitational propagation in the $\Lambda$CDM model including radiation.

hep-th.title: A new class of rotating black hole solutions endowed with a scalar hair
hep-th.author: Hugo Candan, Philippe Grandclement
hep-th.abstract: We present new hairy stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions. These solutions belong to a subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor theories, in which there is no non-minimal coupling to curvature. The full rotating solutions are obtained numerically using the Kadath library based on spectral methods. The metric does not rely on an explicit ansatz but rather on the use of a set of numerical coordinates. Black holes obtained differ from Kerr in general, and depend on a new independent parameter, a primary hair, coming from a linear time dependence in the scalar field. These solutions admit a Killing horizon like the Kerr black hole, but are non-circular, and break the zeroth law of black hole thermodynamics.

hep-th.title: Gravitational fingerprints of a black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity
hep-th.author: Carlos F. S. Pereira, Araújo Filho, Marcos V. de S. Silva, N. Heidari
hep-th.abstract: We investigate particle motion, optical observables, and linear wave propagation around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity with a vanishing cosmological constant. The analysis distinguishes the conserved mass $M$ from the orbital mass $\bar{M}=M/\rho$ and isolates the radial deformation $\sigma^2=1-q/2$, where $q=\ell_2/(1-\ell_1)$. At fixed $\bar{M}$, the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and innermost stable circular orbit retain their Schwarzschild values. Radial frequency ratios also preserve their Schwarzschild profiles for the same areal release and particle radii, while proper distances, infall times, and accumulated orbital angles depend on $\sigma$. For radial fall, the tidal eigenvalues acquire a factor $\sigma^{-2}$, and the instability exponent of the photon orbit scales as $\sigma^{-1}$. In addition, we examine light deflection in the weak and strong regimes with an explicit account of the conical asymptotics. The shadow comparison with Sgr A* and M87* exhibits a coupling degeneracy when the orbital mass and areal distance are set. Scalar, electromagnetic, and massless Dirac perturbations probe the physical metric, whereas a homogeneous axial gravitational sector with $\delta B_{\mu\nu}=0$ admits an exact Schwarzschild spectral map. In this sector, both oscillation and attenuation rates scale as $\sigma^{-1}$ at fixed $\bar{M}$. Third order WKB estimates agree with frequencies extracted from time evolution to within $0.7\%$ for the reported fundamental modes.

hep-th.title: Analytic results for the two-loop renormalization constants of Feynman gauge QED
hep-th.author: Gregory S. Adkins, Elias Mitchell, A. Volkan Turan
hep-th.abstract: The two-loop renormalization constants $Z_m$ and $Z_1\!=\!Z_2$ of Feynman gauge quantum electrodynamics (QED) in the on-shell scheme are computed using dimensional regularization. Analytic results are obtained for these constants. In addition, analytic expressions are obtained for their expansion coefficients in the dimensional regularization parameter $\epsilon$ from order $1/\epsilon^2$ through order $\epsilon^5$. The high-order expansion coefficients will be needed for future multiloop calculations in QED and will provide a useful check for multiloop calculations in QCD.

hep-th.title: Boundary-Sensitive Quantum Order on Non-Amenable Lattices
hep-th.author: Xingzhi Wang, Zohar Nussinov, Gerardo Ortiz
hep-th.abstract: We show that quantum systems on non-amenable lattices, whose boundaries constitute an extensive fraction of the system, host novel forms of bulk ordering with no Euclidean counterpart. Combining boundary-retaining iDMRG with an exact symmetry-fixing duality, we investigate $p<5$ state clock models on the coordination-3 infinite Cayley tree. We find that between the ordered and disordered phases lies an emergent intermediate phase with bulk order induced by an arbitrarily weak boundary field rather than by conventional spontaneous symmetry-breaking. This establishes boundary-sensitive order as a distinct quantum ordering mechanism defying Landau's spontaneous symmetry-breaking paradigm. The intermediate phase realizes a bulk-boundary correspondence in which the unpolarized boundary selects a specific ordered bulk state.

hep-th.title: Axion RG flows and the holographic dynamics of instanton densities
hep-th.author: Yuta Hamada, Elias Kiritsis, Francesco Nitti, Lukas T. Witkowski
hep-th.abstract: Axionic holographic RG flow solutions are studied in the context of general Einstein-Axion-Dilaton theories. A non-trivial axion profile is dual to the (non-perturbative) running of the $\theta$-term for the corresponding instanton density operator. It is shown that a non-trivial axion solution is incompatible with a non-trivial (holographic) IR conformal fixed point. Imposing a suitable axion regularity condition allows to select the IR geometry in a unique way. The solutions are found analytically in the asymptotic UV and IR regimes, and it is shown that in those regimes the axion backreaction is always negligible. The axion backreaction may become important in the intermediate region of the bulk. To make contact with the axion probe limit solutions, a systematic expansion of the solution is developed. Several concrete examples are worked out numerically. It is shown that the regularity condition always implies a finite allowed range for the axion source parameter in the UV. This translates into the existence of a finite (but large) number of saddle-points in the large $N_c$ limit. This ties in well with axion-swampland conjectures.

hep-th.title: $κ$-deformed power spectrum and modified Unruh temperature
hep-th.author: Vishnu Rajagopal
hep-th.abstract: We study the power spectrum of the uniformly accelerating scalar field, obeying the $\kappa$-deformed Klein-Gordon equation. From this we obtain the $\kappa$-deformed corrections to the Unruh temperature, valid up to first order in the $\kappa$-deformation parameter $a$. We also show that in the small acceleration limit, this expression for the Unruh temperature in $\kappa$-deformed space-time is in exact agreement with the one derived from the $\kappa$-deformed uncertainty relation. Finally, we obtain an upper bound on the deformation parameter $a$.

hep-th.title: Brane expansions for anti-symmetric line operator index
hep-th.author: Yosuke Imamura, Masato Inoue
hep-th.abstract: Based on the D5-brane realization of Wilson line operators in anti-symmetric representations, we propose brane expansion formulas for $I_{N,k}$, the Schur index of ${\cal N}=4$ $U(N)$ SYM decorated by line operators in the anti-symmetric representation of rank $k$. For the large $N$ index $I_{\infty,k}$ we propose a double-sum expansion, and for finite $N$ index $I_{N,k}$ we propose a quadruple-sum expansion. Objects causing finite $k$ and finite $N$ corrections are disk D3-branes ending on the D5-brane.

hep-th.title: Holographic free energy and integrated correlators of ${\cal N}=1^*$ theory
hep-th.author: Nakwoo Kim, Hoseob Shin
hep-th.abstract: We consider the 2nd integrated correlators of ${\cal N}=4$, $D=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, especially those which can be associated with ${\cal N}=1^*$ mass-deformed theories. We provide an analytic derivation of the integrals at supergravity tree level, which has not been available so far. Our result agrees with the previous results from the study of BPS solutions in the dual supergravity models.

hep-th.title: Cosmological pole-skipping, shock waves and quantum chaotic dynamics of de Sitter horizons
hep-th.author: Yongjun Ahn, Sašo Grozdanov, Hyun-Sik Jeong, Juan F. Pedraza
hep-th.abstract: We present a systematic analysis of pole-skipping for scalar, Maxwell, and gravitational waves in cosmological spacetimes. Specifically, working in empty de Sitter space and in Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole geometries, we locate the tower of pole-skipping points of such fields and show that they impose nontrivial constraints on the corresponding bulk two-point functions. Focusing on the gravitational sound channel, we then extract the Lyapunov exponent and butterfly velocities that characterize hypothetical dual many-body quantum chaos at each horizon. These chaotic data precisely match the outcome of a gravitational shock wave calculation, confirming that the relevant pole-skipping points encode high-energy scattering of horizon quanta. Interestingly, the butterfly velocities can become superluminal or imaginary, with the latter signaling a spatially modulated propagation of chaos. Assuming that a holographic dual exists, we translate our results into field theory language and propose that the dual theory can be divided into two entangled sectors that capture the black hole and cosmological horizon degrees of freedom. Our results suggest that the black hole sector becomes increasingly nonlocal as the black hole shrinks and that the cosmological horizon sector exhibits behavior compatible with violations of Hermiticity. Finally, we outline simple microscopic toy models, built from long-range and non-Hermitian deformations of the Double Scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (DSSYK)-type chains, that realize these features, providing a concrete arena for future exploration.

hep-th.title: Symmetries, anomalies, and dualities of two-dimensional Non-Linear Sigma Models
hep-th.author: Guillermo Arias-Tamargo, Maxwell L. Velásquez Cotini Hutt
hep-th.abstract: We analyse the global symmetry structure of two-dimensional Non-Linear Sigma Models with Wess-Zumino term. When the target space has a compact isometry without fixed points, the theory has a pair of (group-like) global symmetries and many such theories also have non-invertible symmetries. We describe how the topology of the target space and Wess-Zumino term determine whether the group-like symmetries are continuous or discrete, and study their pure and mixed 't Hooft anomalies. We also revisit the construction of the non-invertible symmetries, which are associated with possible self-dualities under discrete gauging, and show how the global symmetry structure is left invariant by this gauging.

hep-th.title: Differential Equations for Wilson Loops in ABJM Theory
hep-th.author: Takao Suyama
hep-th.abstract: We derive a system of differential equations which are satisfied by the vevs of BPS Wilson loops and 't Hooft coupling of ABJM theory. They are Picard-Fuchs equations of an algebraic curve defined by the derivative of the planar resolvent of the corresponding matrix model. The weak and strong coupling behaviors can be reproduced by their local solutions around regular singularities. We also obtain a recursion relation which can be used to determine the planar vevs of BPS Wilson loops in arbitrary representations.

hep-th.title: Resurgence in scalar and spinor QED: The Euler-Heisenberg Lagrangian in parallel field backgrounds
hep-th.author: Drishti Gupta, Arun Thalapillil
hep-th.abstract: We present the first systematic resurgent analysis of the Euler--Heisenberg Lagrangian in spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics for the most general constant background field configuration. In contrast to the extensively studied case of the perpendicular electric and magnetic fields configuration, the parallel fields configuration exhibits unique asymptotic structures, leading to a substantially richer pattern of singularities in the Borel plane. Explicit large-order asymptotic formulas for the weak-field coefficients in both spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics are derived. These reveal a nontrivial interplay between alternating and non-alternating factorial growth, governed by distinct structures associated with electric and magnetic contributions, and smoothly interpolating between the known perpendicular fields limit. Using Borel--dispersion techniques, we demonstrate that the complete instanton structure underlying Schwinger pair production in parallel fields backgrounds is encoded in the divergent perturbative coefficients. We then construct resurgent approximants using Padé--Borel and Padé--Conformal--Borel resummation schemes adapted to the parallel fields configuration. For the spinor case, conformal improvement results in a significant enhancement in reconstructing both the real and imaginary parts of the effective Lagrangian across a wide range of field ratios. Detailed comparisons with exact special-function representations demonstrate the reliability of reconstructions from a modest number of weak-field coefficients. This work establishes a natural completion of the resurgence programme for constant electromagnetic backgrounds, providing a robust analytic framework for exploring non-perturbative physics and strong-field phenomena in spinor and scalar quantum electrodynamics, from finite perturbative data.

hep-th.title: Combinatorial properties of holographic entropy inequalities
hep-th.author: Guglielmo Grimaldi, Matthew Headrick, Veronika E. Hubeny, Pavel Shteyner
hep-th.abstract: A holographic entropy inequality (HEI) is a linear inequality obeyed by Ryu-Takayanagi holographic entanglement entropies, or equivalently by the minimum cut function on weighted graphs. We establish a new combinatorial framework for studying HEIs, and use it to prove several properties they share, including two majorization-related properties as well as a necessary and sufficient condition for an inequality to be an HEI. We thereby resolve all the conjectures presented in [arXiv:2508.21823], proving two of them and disproving the other two. In particular, we show that the null reduction of any superbalanced HEI passes the majorization test defined in [arXiv:2508.21823], thereby providing strong new evidence that all HEIs are obeyed in time-dependent holographic states.

hep-th.title: The indivisibility of a quantum-corrected AdS black hole with phantom global monopoles
hep-th.author: Tiantong Cheng, Hongbo Cheng
hep-th.abstract: We study the indivisibility of a quantum-corrected AdS black hole involving two kinds of global monopoles, regular or phantom ones to declare the effects from the quantum fluctuation, monopole factors and the negative cosmological constant on the evolution of black holes. We focus our attention on the possibility that this kind of black holes break into their own two parts because of the second law of thermodynamics. We derive and calculate the entropies of the initial black hole and the broken parts respectively and the entropy difference relates to the black holes structure including the quantum-gravity oscillation, global monopoles and the influence from AdS environment. It is found that the two kinds of global monopoles both keep the black holes intact instead of splitting because the entropy difference is negative. The considerable quantum fluctuation compels the defference to be positive and the fragmentation of the black holes may happen in the case that the mass of one fragmented black hole is tiny and the other one's mass is huge. The AdS radius can increase the whole value of change in entropy and the difference near the midpoint of mass ratio will become positive, so the large enough radius may lead the isolated black hole to become two parts nearly equal in the mass.

hep-th.title: Gauge-invariant nonperturbative Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics
hep-th.author: Sorato Nagao, Hiroshi Suzuki
hep-th.abstract: By employing the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG), we study the renormalization group (RG) flow of a manifestly gauge- or Becchi--Rouet--Stora--Tyutin (BRST)-invariant nonperturbative ansatz of the one-particle irreducible (1PI) Wilson action in quantum electrodynamics. The gauge invariance of the Wilson action is \emph{exactly\/} preserved under the RG flow. We explicitly solve the GFERG equation in the leading and partially next-to-leading orders of the large-$N_f$ approximation, where $N_f$ is the number of flavors. We obtain gauge-invariant critical exponents and the gauge-invariant 1PI Wilson action at an infrared (IR) fixed point for~$D<4$, where $D$ is the spacetime dimension.

hep-th.title: Bounds on nonlinear effective field theories via resurgent relative entropy
hep-th.author: Pietro Conzinu, Daiki Ueda
hep-th.abstract: We study a class of nonlinear effective field theories (EFTs) in which relative entropy organizes an infinite tower of higher-dimensional operators with factorially growing coefficients. Using its Borel-resummed expression, we derive bounds on EFT coefficients: under the factorial-growth ansatz, the non-negativity of relative entropy in the weak-background regime constrains the sign of their assumed asymptotic growth, while a negative real part beyond this regime signals perturbative limitations and possible sensitivity to nonperturbative effects. In fermionic QED, analytic continuation from Euclidean to Minkowski spacetime yields a controlled one-loop example: such negativity accompanies the Schwinger instability.

hep-th.title: Quantum spacetime and quantum fluctuations in the IKKT model at weak coupling
hep-th.author: Harold C. Steinacker
hep-th.abstract: This paper aims to clarify conceptual aspects of emergent structure in IKKT-type matrix models. Even without any adjustable parameters in the action, non-trivial matrix vacua do acquire a meaningful coupling constant, as well as two distinct uncertainty scales: a) the scale of noncommutativity of the matrix background, and b) the scale of quantum fluctuations of the matrices under the path integral. These scales are estimated for two prototypes of matrix backgrounds, known as Moyal-Weyl quantum plane and covariant quantum spacetime. Their relative importance separates two regimes: 1) the semi-classical regime interpreted in terms of semi-classical noncommutative geometry, and 2) the deep quantum regime usually interpreted in terms of holography. The quantum fluctuations around the background are shown to be negligible in the weak coupling regime. This justifies a basic assumption in previous work on the emergent 3+1-dimensional semi-classical geometry and (quantum) gravity in suitable vacua.

hep-th.title: Finite-$N$ BMN index across all vacuum sectors
hep-th.author: Chi-Ming Chang, Sarthak Duary, Kangning Liu
hep-th.abstract: We compute the finite-$N$ Witten index of BMN matrix quantum mechanics after summing over all partition-labeled supersymmetric vacuum sectors. Starting from the unitary-matrix integral for each sector, we adapt two complementary evaluation methods to the BMN index: a symmetric-group character expansion, which reduces each fixed fugacity order to a finite combinatorial sum, and a residue expansion in which the contributing poles are organized by rooted trees, with a colored-tree generalization for multi-partition sectors. Where practical, direct integration and extraction of the constant term in the expanded integrand give independent coefficient-by-coefficient checks. We evaluate every vacuum sector for $N\leq 9$. In the equal-fugacity expansion, the coefficients near charges $j\sim N^2$ exhibit substantial cancellations between vacuum sectors, which tend to reduce the effective $N^2$ coefficient of the total index entropy. The finite-$N$ data also reveal a nontrivial sectoral organization: near $j=N^2$, the sector giving the largest contribution changes with $N$, from single-partition sectors at small rank to double-partition sectors starting at $N=6$. We call this phenomenon dominance switching. These results provide quantitative finite-$N$ input for using the BMN index as a diagnostic of protected plane-wave black-hole sectors and suggest in the controlled type-IIA regime a possible D2 dressed black-hole interpretation in which D0 black-hole sectors are accompanied by macroscopic spherical D2-brane degrees of freedom, analogous to dual dressed black holes in $AdS_5\times S^5$.

hep-th.title: New Exotic Operators in the Spectrum of Wilson Lines in General Representations
hep-th.author: Daniele Artico, Carlo Meneghelli, Michele Savi, Rudolfs Treilis
hep-th.abstract: Wilson lines are fundamental probes of gauge theories. We show that, in sufficiently rich representations, they support a large new class of operator insertions. For half-BPS lines in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, some have the quantum numbers of the displacement supermultiplet and define natural defect deformations. By relating their beta-functions to chiral ring OPE coefficients, we show that these deformations are marginally irrelevant, meaning the half-BPS line is IR stable for all representations. We connect these deformations to multidimensional RG flows and find evidence for new conformal line defects.

hep-th.title: Eight-dimensional Manin triples, Yang-Baxter deformations and solutions of Supergravity Equations
hep-th.author: Ladislav Hlavatý, Petr Novotný, Ivo Petr
hep-th.abstract: Extensive list of 4+4-dimensional Manin triples that was presented recently can be used to find new solutions of supergravity equations via Poisson-Lie T-plurality. To get the solutions we start with 1+3-dimensional flat backgrounds on Poisson-Lie groups corresponding to semi-Abelian Manin triples. For application of the Poisson-Lie T-plurality we identify Manin triples that form various decompositions of the same Drinfeld double. Beside flat backgrounds and plane-parallel waves solving supergravity equations, plurality transformation also produces curved backgrounds with torsion satisfying (generalized) supergravity equations. Many of the Poisson-Lie transformations can be understood as homogeneous Yang-Baxter deformations. Of special interest are the non-unimodular deformations leading to solutions of generalized supergravity equations.

hep-th.title: Learning Effective Bulk Fields from Fermionic Spectra: Application to an Extended Power-Law Liquid Model for Cuprate Strange Metals
hep-th.author: Hong-Zhi Xiao, Zhan-Zhi He, Zhuo-Yu Xian, Shao-Feng Wu
hep-th.abstract: We develop a Neural-ODE framework to infer effective bulk metric functions and the charge-weighted gauge potential from boundary fermionic spectra within a static, planar black-hole ansatz. Controlled benchmarks recover the known bulk profiles of the Einstein--Maxwell and Gubser--Rocha models. We then use normalized interaction self-energy targets generated from an extended power-law liquid model with parameters calibrated by angle-resolved photoemission measurements to test the proposed geometric explanation of cuprate strange-metal spectra in a semi-holographic setting. For this application, we use a massless probe in backgrounds with conformal-to-$\mathrm{AdS}_2\times\mathbb{R}^2$ asymptotics and derive a spectral extraction formula from the conserved radial Dirac flux. We identify coordinate/Weyl redundancy and a degeneracy in the scaled Hawking temperature of the normalized inverse problem. The conformal factor remains undetermined, so bulk entropy and the associated contribution to electronic specific heat require independent input. Low-temperature targets are fitted accurately across the studied doping range. In the high-temperature test, however, the present ansatz and optimization search have not yielded a refined geometry that accurately reproduces the thermal spectral shape while preserving frequency symmetry. These results may guide the further development of semi-holographic models for cuprates, and the framework may also find applications in other strongly correlated electron systems.

hep-th.title: Kaluza-Klein tower thresholds and scheme dependence of the species scale
hep-th.author: Yuri Michinobu
hep-th.abstract: We revisit the species scale in quantum gravity from the viewpoint of effective field theory (EFT). Two common parametric characterizations relate it to the breakdown of perturbative gravity and to the suppression scale of higher-derivative gravitational operators. We examine their correspondence through local threshold corrections from infinite Kaluza-Klein (KK) towers. In four dimensions, we compute the four-derivative one-loop action of minimally coupled scalar and Dirac towers with KK spectra in graviton, radion, and photon backgrounds. Feynman diagrams determine the single-mode coefficients, while analytic summation with full threshold functions tests the logarithmic coefficient inferred from renormalization-group evolution. The leading contribution scales with the effective number of KK levels, reproducing the standard species-scale relation under the stated matching assumptions, but its coefficient depends on the cutoff profile and belongs to EFT matching data. In contrast, the subleading curvature-squared thresholds contain logarithms of the KK mass gap whose spin-dependent coefficients remain stable under changes of the cutoff profile within the class studied here.

hep-th.title: Holograms and Standard Models
hep-th.author: Shoichiro Miyashita, Yasuhiro Sekino, Leonard Susskind
hep-th.abstract: Despite riddles, mysteries, and enigmas the theory of elementary particles has not changed for 50 years. We argue that the current paradigm -- Wilsonian quantum field theory -- is inadequate for resolving the puzzles, and should be replaced by a new paradigm based on the Holographic Principle. We show how a simplified but still very rich standard model emerges from de Sitter holography in the flat-space limit and explain why the puzzle of huge quantum corrections to the cosmological constant simply does not occur in the holographic paradigm.

hep-th.title: Massive Graviton Dark Matter from a Gapped Continuum
hep-th.author: Eugenio Megias, Miguel Prieto, Mariano Quiros
hep-th.abstract: We consider the possibility of dark matter in a warped extra-dimensional theory in the presence of a linear dilaton background, with a gapped continuum spectrum, in a brane-world cosmological scenario. Firstly, triggered by self-energy radiative corrections, we study the existence of an isolated resonance of massive gravitons, and its realization as a long-lived feebly interacting dark matter candidate, produced by the freeze-in mechanism. This massive graviton is proved to satisfy all theoretical and experimental constraints, in the sub-MeV mass range. We further consider the close relationship between the existence of this component of dark matter and the presence of an inflaton localized on the brane, with a mass around $10^{11}$ GeV and a sub-TeV reheating temperature, in a brane inflationary scenario that allows one to reproduce the most recent cosmological observables. Secondly, the gapped continuum of gravitons, a particular five-dimensional realization of the physics of unparticles, is identified as a holographic fluid which can play the role of holographic dark matter. The production of the holographic fluid goes by an ultraviolet freeze-in mechanism, with an abundance mainly depending on the reheating temperature. Depending on the values of the mass gap and the reheating temperature, one or both components of dark matter can be present.

hep-th.title: Decoupling Limit of Quiver Theories and the Angular Spectra of Extreme C-metrics
hep-th.author: Peng Yang, Kilar Zhang
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the angular eigenvalue problem of the extreme charged C-metric. Starting from a constrained five-point Fuchsian description of the non-extremal angular equation, we obtain its extreme limit by decoupling a hypermultiplet in the dual four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$, $\mathrm{SU(2)}\times \mathrm{SU(2)}$ linear quiver gauge theory. We derive the parameter dictionary and renormalized Matone relations, and connect the physical limit $Q\to M$ to the quiver decoupling by an explicit coordinate transformation. Regular endpoint conditions give an algebraic quantization condition. Eigenvalues obtained from the truncated instanton prepotential are tested against independent angular spectra near extremality and at larger acceleration. The axisymmetric sector recovers the known exact spectrum.

hep-th.title: Leading Yukawa terms in the three-loop anomalous dimension and four-loop $β$-function of ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theories for various renormalization prescriptions
hep-th.author: Ratmir Jumanov, Konstantin Stepanyantz
hep-th.abstract: For an arbitrary renormalizable ${\cal N}=1$ supersymmetric theory with a single gauge coupling regularized by higher covariant derivatives we calculate the three-loop contribution to the anomalous dimension of the matter superfields proportional to the sixth powers of Yukawa couplings for a wide class of renormalization prescriptions. Next, taking into account that in the case of using the higher covariant derivatives supplemented by minimal subtractions of logarithms the NSVZ relation is valid in all orders, we calculate the corresponding four-loop contribution to the gauge $\beta$-function and investigate its scheme dependence. In particular, we construct the so-called ``minimal'' renormalization prescription for which the renormalization group functions have the simplest possible form provided that the exact equations for the gauge and Yukawa $\beta$-functions following from supersymmetry remain valid.

hep-th.title: Fibre Inflation Beyond BHP: Constraints and a BHP-Free Regime
hep-th.author: Xin Gao, Zhiwei Li, Chuying Wang
hep-th.abstract: We study a restricted fibre-dependent $\alpha'$-loop sector in Type IIB Large Volume Scenario fibre inflation beyond the conventional Berg-Haack-Pajer (BHP) parametrisation. Motivated by effective-field-theory corrections in K3-fibred Calabi--Yau orientifolds, we analyse BHP-complete, partially BHP-driven and BHP-free configurations. For BHP-driven cases, the additional corrections act as effective deformations of the standard fibre potential and are bounded at the percent level relative to the corresponding BHP structures, with logarithmic terms typically more restricted due to their effects on the slope and curvature. At the effective-field-theory level, we identify a BHP-free fibre-inflation regime, referred to as $\alpha'$-loop inflation, in which the conventional KK- and winding-type BHP channels vanish while the generalized loop sector stabilises the fibre modulus and supports slow-roll inflation. This regime exhibits a characteristic hierarchy between fibre-dependent loop structures controlled by the large-volume suppression and satisfies CMB, Kähler-cone, large-volume and heavy-modulus constraints. Our results show that fibre inflation is sensitive to the orientifold and brane configurations, and that corrections beyond the BHP ansatz can generate new controlled inflationary regimes.

hep-th.title: MacDowell-Mansouri $σ$-model
hep-th.author: Egor Pluzhnikov, Stanislav Alexeyev
hep-th.abstract: Standard pre-geometric mechanisms reproduce the $\Lambda$CDM model but lack a natural source for inflation. We propose a mechanism for the emergence of scalar-coupled topological terms by extending the Lie algebra of a MacDowell-Mansouri model to a Lie algebroid. These terms are commonly regarded as a source for cosmological inflation in effective string actions. With an additional constraint on torsion imposed, the theory reduces to a scalar-tensor theory belonging to the Horndeski class, and reproduces inflationary dynamics that meet existing constraints (Planck/BICEP/Keck and GW170817).

hep-th.title: Cohomological Aspects of Entanglement Entropy: From Information Theory to Noncommutative Geometry
hep-th.author: R. C. Rashkov
hep-th.abstract: We develop a cohomological framework for entanglement entropy that unifies information theory, operator algebras, and noncommutative geometry. Entropy is a 1-cocycle in information cohomology; we generalize this to the quantum setting via Hochschild and cyclic cohomology. For an inclusion of von Neumann algebras N contained in M with a faithful normal state w admitting a cyclic and separating vector, and a conditional expectation E: M -> N (whose existence is equivalent to modular invariance of N by Takesaki's theorem), we construct the entanglement complex as the image of the transgression map tau_w on the relative cyclic complex, where A is a dense *-subalgebra of M and B = A intersect N. Our main result identifies entanglement cohomology with the kernel of the restriction map HC*(A) -> HC*(B), up to the connecting homomorphism d of the long exact sequence of the pair (A,B); when d = 0, the identification is exact. The relative modular cocycle u_t = (Dw : D(w|_N) o E)_t generates explicit entanglement classes when E is not w-invariant, with the Araki relative entropy as its infinitesimal generator. The framework accommodates Type III von Neumann algebras, where no local density matrix exists, and leads to a holographic proposal: a subspace of H^1_ent is conjecturally dual to linearized modular Hamiltonian perturbations of the bulk entanglement wedge. We verify the construction in finite-dimensional, type II_1, and type III_1 examples.

hep-th.title: Conformal blocks and braiding matrices for RCFTs I: Virasoro minimal models
hep-th.author: Suresh Govindarajan, Aditya Jain, Akhila Sadanandan, Prasanta K. Tripathy
hep-th.abstract: We develop a systematic method for computing the braiding matrices of four-point functions in RCFTs. This is implemented for the case of Virasoro minimal models. The first few terms of the conformal block series are directly computed through the Shapovalov form. The Fuchsian (BPZ) ODEs for order three and higher have accessory parameters that are fixed by this direct computation. We thus bypass the derivation from the null-state condition which gets tedious for higher-level null states. The braiding F-matrices are connection matrices between the Frobenius solutions at two singular points of the ODE. The F-matrices are computed numerically at first, agreeing with the results of Dotsenko--Fateev, which uses the Coulomb-gas formalism. We find that after a change of basis, the F-matrix is rendered unitary, which determines (products of) the three-point structure constants. We conjecture that the squares of the entries of the unitary F-matrix lie in a cyclotomic extension of the rational numbers. This enables us to convert our numerical estimates for the F-matrix into exact ones. The formalism is illustrated through numerous examples in Virasoro minimal models. We also discuss how these methods can be extended to cases involving symmetries that extend the Virasoro symmetry as well as for tenable examples that arise from the holomorphic modular bootstrap program.

hep-th.title: Quantum vacuum inversion and multi-kink unbinding in the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model
hep-th.author: Jonathan Lozano-Mayo
hep-th.abstract: Quantum fluctuations can unbind a composite soliton while the correction to its mass stays small. We show this beyond perturbation theory for the multi-kinks of the non-degenerate double sine-Gordon model. At one loop the vacuum at the centre of the multi-kink becomes the true vacuum at a coupling of order the classical lifting of the vacua. Tensor-network calculations of the lattice theory show that this inversion survives beyond one loop and has a continuum limit, and that the Gaussian effective potential captures it. On finite chains the multi-kink unbinds when the tension of the string of central vacuum between its two halves falls through zero

hep-th.title: 3d Lovelock gravity and the holographic c-theorem: Proof at all orders and resummation
hep-th.author: Gokhan Alkac, Luis Guajardo, Hikmet Ozsahin
hep-th.abstract: We prove that 3d Lovelock gravity, the Horndeski theory obtained from the regularized Lovelock invariants in three dimensions, admits a holographic c-theorem at all orders and for arbitrary values of the couplings. In the minisuperspace of domain wall solutions, the equation of the Horndeski scalar is a total derivative at every order, which locks the derivative of the scalar to that of the warp factor along the flows we consider and allows the null energy condition to be integrated into a monotonic c-function. The linear scalar profile of the resulting vacuum breaks the special conformal transformations, so the dual theory is scale-invariant but not conformal, and the central charge is defined as the coefficient of the logarithmic divergence of the on-shell action on the sphere. We compute it exactly for the Gauss-Bonnet case and asymptotically for the full tower, and find that it is linear in the couplings and matches the UV value of the c-function. Since all results depend on the couplings only through two generating functions, we give the resummed Lagrangians, c-functions and central charges in closed form for the choices of couplings that lead to regular black holes, and classify the resummed theories by the positivity of the effective Newton constant on the vacuum and the uniqueness of the vacuum with a non-trivial scalar.

hep-th.title: DSSYK, open ASEP/TASEP and 2d dilaton gravity at strong coupling
hep-th.author: Alexander Gorsky, Elizaveta Kovalenko, Sergei Nechaev
hep-th.abstract: We discuss the triality between stochastic growth models in the KPZ universality class, the DSSYK model, and low dimensional dilaton gravity. The TASEP model, which will be our primary focus, is identified with the strong-coupling limit of two-dimensional quantum gravity. The Hamiltonian of DSSYK and the transfer matrix of ASEP coincide up to an additive constant, and we derive the exact expression for the resolvent of the corresponding transfer matrix in ASEP on a finite interval. We also mention the relation of cumulants with the Tutte polynomial $T(1,q)$ of the crossing graph dual to the chord diagram, which implies the relationship of the models considered with the $Q=0$ Potts model coupled with gravity. We further exploit the realization of all these models in terms of different versions of discrete and continuous random walks on two-dimensional manifolds, which parameterize the Hilbert spaces of the respective theories. The representation of TASEP as the growth model of heaps provides new insight into strong-coupling gravity, suggesting its interpretation as an emerging phenomenon. The new dualities between ASEP and q-TASEP models and heap models providing a useful growth interpretation have been developed.

hep-th.title: The Cosmological $δ$-shift
hep-th.author: Carolina Figueiredo, Jiajie Mei, Yuyu Mo, Francisco Vazão
hep-th.abstract: We consider the extension of the $\delta$-shift connecting Tr$(\phi^3)$ and pion amplitudes to observables in cosmology. We start in flat-space and explain how one can extract the pion wavefunction and correlators from those of Tr$(\phi^3)$ theory, via a simple kinematic deformation. As opposed to the amplitude, the $\delta$-shift for the wavefunction is no longer a linear deformation on the kinematics since the wavefunction depends on magnitudes rather than the squares of momenta. We "linearize" this deformation by using the frequency representation - allowing us to recast the contribution from any graph as a sum over residues. We then show how this construction extends to de Sitter, and find that, remarkably, in the frequency representation, the pion de Sitter wavefunction and correlators can be formulated in precisely the same way as in flat-space. Amongst other things, this unified formulation reveals a simple universal soft-limit for flat-space and de Sitter, where, in the soft-limit, the wavefunction turns into a sum of wavefunctions in a mixed theory of pions and scalars.

hep-th.title: Reconstructing BPS String Charge Cone in 6d N=(1,0) Supergravity
hep-th.author: Yuta Hamada, Hee-Cheol Kim, Kai Xu
hep-th.abstract: The tensor branch of six-dimensional $\mathcal N=(1,0)$ supergravity is characterized by a spectrum of BPS strings charged under the two-form gauge fields. Their charges span a cone in the tensor charge lattice, whose extremal rays are generated by primitive BPS string charges that become tensionless at the boundaries of the tensor moduli space. We develop a systematic procedure, based entirely on effective field theory data, to reconstruct the primitive BPS string generators and thereby determine the complete closed BPS string cone of any 6d $(1,0)$ supergravity theory. The key ingredients are the universal {\it H}-string, which allows us to isolate a fixed sector determined by classified LST blocks and gauge anomaly data from the remaining gauge-neutral E-string sector, and a BPS refinement of the Completeness Conjecture that ensures population of the relevant charge rays. We further show that this reconstruction provides new constraints on the low-energy theory and can rule out candidate EFTs that pass all previously known local lattice and anomaly consistency conditions. Separately, for theories admitting geometric tensor bases, we explain how the same reconstruction determines the complete Mori cone of the corresponding Kähler surface.

hep-th.title: Surface defects in $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills: exact results and holographic bootstrap
hep-th.author: Lorenzo Bianchi, Davide Bonomi, Maddalena Ferragatta, Valentina Forini
hep-th.abstract: We study two-point functions of chiral primary operators in $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills in the presence of a half-BPS surface defect. Such a defect preserves only the diagonal combination of transverse rotations and of a global U(1) R-symmetry, so that the correlator depends on one additional cross-ratio and splits into sectors of definite angular charge. We solve the superconformal Ward identities and construct the bulk and defect superconformal blocks in all sectors, including the charged ones, which have no analogue for defects preserving transverse rotations. The solution contains a holomorphic sector, which we fix non-perturbatively by mapping it to a chiral algebra correlator. We extend this map to defects breaking transverse rotations, where it requires a redefinition of the modes of the two-dimensional current algebra, and use it to fix the charged sectors as well. We then use the defect dispersion relation to reconstruct the full correlator of the dimension-two chiral primary at leading order at large N and strong coupling. In the charged sectors long multiplets are absent and the answer is conjecturally exact in both N and the coupling; expanding it at weak coupling, we find perfect agreement with known results. From these correlators we extract infinitely many new pieces of defect CFT data. Finally, we reproduce the strong-coupling answer by an independent Witten diagram bootstrap on the rotation-invariant locus.

hep-th.title: Multipartite Entanglement Geometry in AdS/BCFT
hep-th.author: Debarshi Basu, Qiang Wen, Mingshuai Xu
hep-th.abstract: Multipartite entanglement measures probe how quantum correlations are organized beyond what can be inferred from pairwise entropies. We study how this structure is reshaped by a physical boundary in a holographic BCFT. The end-of-the-world brane opens new relative-homology channels for multipartite entanglement, allowing connected bulk webs to reorganize and factorize at scales that need not coincide with any ordinary Ryu--Takayanagi transition. In static AdS$_3$/BCFT$_2$, this produces a characteristic hierarchy of multipartite phases and a nontrivial dependence of genuine multi-entropy on the boundary. In the thermofield-double state, genuinely connected webs can instead be supported through the Einstein--Rosen bridge, leading to growth, reconnection and saturation scales distinct from the usual Hartman--Maldacena transitions. These results show that multipartite entanglement is sensitive not only to extremal-surface areas but also to how bulk entanglement structures are allowed to join, split and terminate in the presence of a boundary.

hep-th.title: Probability measures for de Sitter JT gravity
hep-th.author: Wilfried Buchmuller, Alexander Westphal
hep-th.abstract: Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity with positive cosmological constant is a toy model to study the emergence of expanding de Sitter universes from a quantum state. Its density matrix is a superposition of double-trumpet amplitudes which are solutions of a Wheeler-DeWitt equation. We compare predictions of such mixed states for classical expanding universes with the corresponding predictions of no-boundary wavefunctions. Double-trumpet amplitudes consistent with holography, whose semiclassical limit matches the result from Schwarzian boundary fluctuations, lead to a flat probability distribution for the size of the universe, consistent with models of inflation. This is in contrast to the suppression of large universes predicted by no-boundary wave functions.

hep-th.title: About P-adic Numbers and Professor Igor Volovich on the Occasion of his 80th Anniversary
hep-th.author: Paul H Frampton
hep-th.abstract: We recall a 1987 paper written by Volovich and our subsequent work with Okada which established the Feyman rules for the p-adic string and the related non-local field theory which found diverse physical applications. We add some memories of visits to Moscow during 1989-91.

hep-th.title: Krylov complexity and oscillatory quantum dynamics in two-field inflation
hep-th.author: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu, Hai-Bing Fu
hep-th.abstract: We investigate Krylov-space dynamics of primordial perturbations in two-field inflation. Starting from the quadratic action for coupled curvature and entropy perturbations, we solve the mode equations with Bunch-Davies initial conditions and construct the corresponding quadratic Hamiltonian. The Gaussian quantum state is described by a four-mode squeezed state with two squeezing channels. We derive the evolution of the squeezing strength and squeezing angle and use them to evaluate the Krylov complexity, Krylov entropy, and channel-resolved Lanczos coefficients. Our numerical results show that the two channels remain weakly squeezed inside the horizon but develop different squeezing histories after horizon exit. The second channel develops strong squeezing earlier and dominates the intermediate evolution, whereas the first channel shows a delayed enhancement. The corresponding Krylov complexities exhibit distinct oscillatory structures across horizon crossing and pronounced fluctuations in the strongly squeezed superhorizon regime. These features arise from the phase-sensitive squeezing dynamics and reflect the different responses of the two channels to curvature-entropy coupling.

hep-th.title: Multi-pole extension for elliptic models of interacting integrable tops
hep-th.author: E. Trunina, A. Zotov
hep-th.abstract: We review and give detailed description for ${\rm gl}_{NM}$ Gaudin models related to holomorphic vector bundles of rank $NM$ and degree $M$ over elliptic curve with $n$ punctures. Then we introduce their generalizations constructed by means of $R$-matrices satisfying the associative Yang-Baxter equation. A natural extension of the obtained models to the Schlesinger systems is given as well.

hep-th.title: Quantum superposition of black hole states as a communication resource
hep-th.author: Richard Howl, Ali Akil, Hlér Kristjánsson, Xiaobin Zhao, Giulio Chiribella
hep-th.abstract: The interplay between black holes and quantum information has revealed deep connections between gravity and quantum mechanics. For example, the classical spacetime geometry of a black hole has been shown to degrade quantum entanglement shared by nearby observers, one of whom is in free fall. Here we examine how this picture changes when the black hole's mass degrees of freedom are allowed to exist in a coherent quantum superposition, corresponding to a superposition of distinct spacetime geometries. We show that such quantum coherence can mitigate the loss of entanglement between nearby observers, thereby enhancing the performance of quantum communication protocols operating in the vicinity of the black hole.

hep-th.title: Lax equations for relativistic ${\rm GL}(NM,{\mathbb C})$ Gaudin models on elliptic curve
hep-th.author: E. Trunina, A. Zotov
hep-th.abstract: We describe the most general ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ classical elliptic finite-dimensional integrable system, which Lax matrix has $n$ simple poles on elliptic curve. For $M=1$ it reproduces the classical inhomogeneous spin chain, for $N=1$ it is the Gaudin type (multispin) extension of the spin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model, and for $n=1$ the model of $M$ interacting relativistic ${\rm GL}_N$ tops emerges in some particular case. In this way we present a classification for relativistic Gaudin models on ${\rm GL}$-bundles over elliptic curve. As a by-product we describe the inhomogeneous Ruijsenaars chain. We show that this model can be considered as a particular case of multispin Ruijsenaars-Schneider model when residues of the Lax matrix are of rank one. An explicit parametrization of the classical spin variables through the canonical variables is obtained for this model. Finally, the most general ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ model is also described through $R$-matrices satisfying associative Yang-Baxter equation. This description provides the trigonometric and rational analogues of ${\rm GL}_{NM}$ models.

hep-th.title: From vertex operator superalgebras to graded-local conformal nets and back
hep-th.author: Sebastiano Carpi, Tiziano Gaudio, Robin Hillier
hep-th.abstract: We generalize the Carpi-Kawahigashi-Longo-Weiner correspondence between vertex operator algebras and conformal nets to the case of vertex operator superalgebras and graded-local conformal nets by introducing the notion of strongly graded-local vertex operator superalgebra. Then we apply our machinery to a number of well-known examples including superconformal field theory models. We also prove that all lattice VOSAs are strongly graded-local. Furthermore, we prove strong graded-locality of the super-Moonshine VOSA, whose group of automorphisms preserving the superconformal structure is isomorphic to Conway's largest sporadic simple group, and of the shorter Moonshine VOSA, whose automorphisms group is isomorphic to the direct product of the baby Monster with a cyclic group of order two.

hep-th.title: Gravitational waves from cosmic superstrings and gauge strings
hep-th.author: Danny Marfatia, Ye-Ling Zhou
hep-th.abstract: We perform a phenomenological comparison of the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum expected from cosmic gauge string networks and superstring networks comprised of multiple string types. We show how violations of scaling behavior and the evolution of the number of relativistic degrees of freedom in the early Universe affect the GW spectrum. We derive simple analytical expressions for the GW spectrum from superstrings and gauge strings that are valid for all frequencies relevant to pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and laser interferometers. We analyze the latest data from PTAs and show that superstring networks are consistent with 32 nHz data from NANOGrav, but are excluded by 3.2 nHz data at $3\sigma$ unless the string coupling $g_s<0.2$ or the strings evolve in only about 10% of the volume of the higher-dimensional space. We also point out that while gauge string networks are excluded by NANOGrav-15 data at $3\sigma$, they are completely compatible with EPTA and PPTA data. Finally, we study correlations between GW signals at PTAs and laser interferometers.

hep-th.title: Unruh effect using Doppler shift method in DSR framework
hep-th.author: Vishnu Rajagopal
hep-th.abstract: We study the Unruh effect in doubly special relativity (DSR) framework by generalising the Doppler-shift method to DSR. For both the scalar and Dirac particles, we observe a deviation in the power spectrum of Unruh radiation from the standard Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac distributions, respectively, due to the presence of the frame independent length scale of DSR. We further show that this deviation results in the modification of Unruh temperature which then depends non-linearly on the proper acceleration in DSR.

hep-th.title: Classical Simulability from Operator Entanglement Scaling
hep-th.author: Neil Dowling
hep-th.abstract: Local-operator entanglement (LOE) quantifies the nonlocal structure of Heisenberg operators and serves as a diagnostic of many-body chaos. We provide rigorous bounds showing when an operator can be well-approximated by a matrix-product operator (MPO), given asymptotic scaling of its LOE $\alpha$-Rényi entropies. Specifically, we prove that a volume law scaling for $\alpha\geq 1$ implies that the operator cannot be approximated efficiently as an MPO while faithfully reproducing all expectation values. On the other hand, if we restrict to correlations over a relevant sub-class of (ensembles of) states, then logarithmic scaling of the $\alpha < 1$ entropies implies MPO simulability. This result covers a range of relevant quantities, including infinite temperature autocorrelation functions, out-of-time-ordered correlators, and average-case expectation values over ensembles of computational basis states. Beyond this regime, we provide numerical evidence together with a random matrix model to argue that this simulability result also typically holds for arbitrary states. Our results put on firm footing the heuristic expectation that a low operator entanglement implies efficient tensor network representability, extending celebrated foundational results from the theory of matrix-product states and providing a formal link between quantum chaos and classical simulability.

hep-th.title: Physics inspired quantum algorithm for QCD splitting functions
hep-th.author: Gabriel Rouxinol, Yacine Haddad, Cenk Tüysüz, Sofia Vallecorsa, Michele Grossi
hep-th.abstract: We introduce a modular quantum circuit primitive to model entanglement dynamics in QCD parton splitting and use it as a composable building block for data-driven, physics-consistent modelling of parton-shower kinematics. For the pure-gluon channel, we derive an analytic expression for the helicity entanglement generated at the splitting vertex, quantified via the concurrence, and construct a two-qubit circuit whose $\sigma_3$ expectation values encode the momentum shared between outgoing gluons. The circuit reproduces the QCD-predicted concurrence by construction, which fixes a two-qubit correlator that the momentum fractions alone do not determine. Iterating the primitive, the concurrence obeys a product rule across successive splittings. Calibrating the circuit parameters to LHC jet substructure data relates the reconstructed momentum-sharing fractions directly to circuit rotation angles. Composing multiple splitting primitives yields multi-prong momentum-fraction distributions; we compare the three- and four-prong cases against experimental data, reproducing the core of the distributions. For the three-prong configuration, we execute the circuit on superconducting quantum hardware, recover the momentum-fraction distributions after a device-bias correction calibrated on a held-out subset, and study how noise alters the entanglement-dependent observable. This work provides a concrete framework for quantum-native parton-shower modules that encode quantum correlations at the level of splitting dynamics, and offers physics-informed ansätze for future quantum algorithms for QCD.

hep-th.title: Demagnetizing KBR and New Ricci-flat Rotating Metric
hep-th.author: Liang Ma, H.Lu
hep-th.abstract: We construct a new Ricci-flat metric by demagnetizing the recently reported Kerr-Bertotti-Robinson (KBR) solution. The metric is a deformation of the Kerr metric characterized by a parameter $B$, so that the asymptotic Kerr becomes a regular dome of spindle shape with north and south poles. Despite lacking an asymptotically-flat region, we find that the first law of black hole thermodynamics can be established. Some thermodynamic relations are identical to those of the Kerr black hole, as if the constant $B$ is absent. Our Ricci-flat rotating metric serves a neutral seed for a variety of inequivalent schemes of magnetizing the Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes.

hep-th.title: Stochastic scalar-tensor inflation and beyond
hep-th.author: Yoann Launay
hep-th.abstract: During cosmological inflation, inhomogeneities arising from quantum vacuum fluctuations are stretched to become super-Hubble and effectively classical. As many scenarios of the origin involve nonlinearities or a breakdown of perturbativity in the infrared, the limitations of quantum field theory can be addressed using a stochastic description of the dynamics, the so-called stochastic inflation paradigm. However, the stochastic formalism was only recently formulated consistently within full General Relativity and has not yet been extended to more general theories of the early universe, which is the subject of this work.In order to find the stochastic sources for a wide class of fully nonlinear scalar-tensor theories, we apply our gauge-agnostic coarse-graining procedure to the linear equations of the associated effective field theory. Each theory can then be mapped to its own set of stochastic equations of motion by identifying the corresponding coefficients in the former. We illustrate this with a few concrete and, in most cases, unprecedented examples, including Gauss-Bonnet, generalized Brans-Dicke, Horndeski, and braiding theories.Finally, we discuss other natural extensions to provide a phenomenologically complete stochastic framework. For example, we showcase the coarse-graining of multifield inflation in full General Relativity and argue for the generality of our procedure and thus its potential applications beyond the realm of inflation.

hep-th.title: Regular Black Holes from Anisotropic Source with Hydrodynamic Equation of State
hep-th.author: Hassan Firouzjahi
hep-th.abstract: We study regular black hole solutions sourced by an anisotropic energy momentum tensor. It is well known that the geometry of the interior of a spherically symmetric regular black hole approaches the dS metric. Having decomposed the energy momentum tensor into its isotropic and anisotropic components, we assume a hydrodynamic equation of state, $P= P(\rho)$, for the pressure, and look for spherically symmetric, regular black hole solutions. We consider different forms of $ P(\rho)$ which yield the previously known regular black hole solutions, as well as various new metrics. We show that the profile of $ P(\rho)$ has a root and a maximum as it approaches $0^+$ at large distances. Consequently, the square of the sound speed of perturbations, $c_s^2$, changes sign at the point where $P$ reaches its maximum, indicating a potential hydrodynamic instability. In addition, imposing the subluminal bound on $c_s$ puts strong constraints on the model parameters, excluding models in which the energy density has an exponential fall off. We establish a universal hierarchy among the relative positions at which the strong energy condition is violated, at which $P$ has its root, and at which $P$ attains its maximum.

hep-th.title: Spin-mediated modulation of chaos bound violation in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes
hep-th.author: Chuang Yang, Deyou Chen, Bingbing Chen
hep-th.abstract: In this paper, we investigate how the particle spin modulates chaos bound violations in Lorentz-violating black hole spacetimes within the framework of Bumblebee gravity. Using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon formalism, we analyze the effects of spin-curvature coupling, Lorentz symmetry breaking, and the cosmological constant on the orbital instability in static spherically symmetric (A)dS black holes. We find that the particle spin provides an additional mechanism for modulating the critical angular momentum associated with the onset of violation. The Lorentz-violating parameter suppresses the violations by reducing the accessible parameter space and the critical charge. Meanwhile, a negative cosmological constant decreases the violation region but enhances the violation magnitude for allowed configurations. Our results demonstrate that the spin and Lorentz symmetry breaking jointly regulate the interplay between orbital instability and black hole horizon properties.

hep-th.title: Langlands Duality and Invariant Differential Operators: the Case SL(2n+1)
hep-th.author: V.K. Dobrev
hep-th.abstract: Recently we started building a bridge between two cases of Langlands duality. The latter is one of the most influential topics in mathematical research. It has many different appearances and influential subtopics. Yet there is a topic that until now seems unrelated to the Langlands program. That is the topic of invariant differential operators. That is strange since both items are deeply rooted in Harish-Chandra's representation theory of semisimple Lie groups. We started with the case of the group ~$SL(2n)$. In the present paper we deal with the group $SL(2n+1)$. The two mentioned groups are similar, but their representation theories is rather different.

hep-th.title: Spectral Localization in Cavity-Mediated Entanglement Harvesting
hep-th.author: Hao Xu
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the relation between spectral localization and entanglement harvesting in an analytically solvable model of two qubits coupled to a leaky single-mode cavity, which in turn couples to a continuous electromagnetic bath. We derive the no-jump concurrence at a prescribed reference gate time in closed form, $\mathcal C_g(Q)=2e^{-\pi/(2Q)}(1+e^{-\pi/(2Q)})/(1+3e^{-\pi/Q})$, where $Q\equiv|\Delta|/\kappa$ is the ratio of the qubit-cavity detuning $\Delta$ to the cavity linewidth $\kappa$. This reference time is inherited from the first maximally entangling unitary gate. At finite loss, $\mathcal C_g$ is the conditional concurrence at this prescribed readout time. In the high-$Q$ limit, $\mathcal C_g\simeq1-\pi^2/(16Q^2)$, while in the low-$Q$ limit it decays exponentially. For the Lorentzian spectral family, $Q$ is proportional to a detuning-normalized inverse participation ratio and simultaneously measures the balance between coherent exchange and collective decay. This yields a compact, model-specific description of the crossover from nearly unit conditional entanglement to overdamped suppression. The predicted $\mathcal C_g(Q)$ curve can, in principle, be examined in circuit QED with ideal monitoring and no-jump post-selection.

hep-th.title: Galois descents of certain multiple polylogarithms
hep-th.author: Yajun Zhou
hep-th.abstract: We prove some conjectures of K. C. Au concerning the descents of cyclotomic levels in certain sums over multiple polylogarithms. Via answers to a question of Au in some particular cases, we also confirm Broadhurst's conjecture on honorary multiple zeta values at even weights.

hep-th.title: The onset of the strong backreaction regime in axion inflation, an analytical study
hep-th.author: Aditya Kulkarni, Lorenzo Sorbo
hep-th.abstract: Models where an axion-like inflaton is coupled to a $U(1)$ gauge field are theoretically well motivated and can display a rich phenomenology. The regime in which the quanta of the gauge field strongly backreact on the rolling inflaton has been studied for well more than a decade, and yet we cannot say that it is fully understood. In this paper we present an analytical study of the onset of the strong backreaction regime. Our formalism relies on a Laplace transform to convert a complicated integro-differential equation into the search of the poles of an analytic function. We confirm the existence, previously observed using a completely different formalism, of a stable region of strong backreaction. Our work provides, for the first time, analytical formulae that allow to study the evolution of the system as it transitions from the weak to the strong backreaction regime.

hep-th.title: A computer assisted existence proof for a non-Schwarzschild black hole in Einstein--Weyl gravity
hep-th.author: Kevin Goldstein, Vishnu Jejjala
hep-th.abstract: Static, asymptotically flat, non-Schwarzschild black holes in four-dimensional Einstein--Weyl gravity have previously been constructed by numerical shooting, while the local field equations admit horizon and asymptotic expansions to all orders. We give a computer assisted existence proof for a non-Schwarzschild solution whose dimensionless horizon radius is one in units of the massive spin-two scale, with parameters close to the previously reported numerical branch. The exterior is divided into a convergent horizon series domain, a compact core enclosed by a parameter dependent Taylor model with directed rounding, and an infinite asymptotic domain treated as a centered stable manifold fixed point problem. The resulting five-dimensional matching map between the core and tail is continuous on a rigorously specified box. After exact rational preconditioning, the signs on opposite faces satisfy the hypotheses of the Poincaré--Miranda theorem and therefore certify a matching zero. The solution has a regular nondegenerate horizon, no additional exterior horizon, vanishing Ricci scalar, and nonvanishing Ricci tensor. The strict bounds also imply existence at every sufficiently nearby horizon radius and a local continuous family at fixed coupling. The proof establishes existence, but not uniqueness of the matching zero.

hep-th.title: A Hopf Algebraic Theory of the Quantum Magnusian
hep-th.author: Li Guo, Joon-Hwi Kim, Jung-Wook Kim, Sungsoo Kim, Sangmin Lee, Jian-Rong Li
hep-th.abstract: We develop a Hopf-algebraic theory of graph coefficients arising in the quantum Magnus expansion. At the classical level, the expansion is governed by directed trees, whereas its quantum counterpart involves loop graphs, multiple edges, and several types of edge data. We introduce a contraction Hopf algebra of mixed quivers containing these diagrams and closed under contraction.On this algebra we define a character $e$ from normalized linear-extension data, directed-tadpole factors, and a prescription for undirected edges, and let $\omega$ be its convolution inverse. Our main result is a universal closed formula for the connected function $\omega_c$ on every finite mixed quiver, expressed as a finite sum over ordered set partitions of the vertices. We also construct a weighted vertex-splitting Hopf structure on the unlocalized mixed-quiver algebra, with convolution $\star_V$ and canonical edge-weight character $\zeta_V$, such that $\omega_c=\log_{\star_V}\zeta_V$. Compatibility of the two coproducts and an explicit identity between their characters explain this equality. We further prove that the two-vertex contraction identity, tadpole factorization, vanishing on disconnected graphs, and boundary data uniquely determine $\omega_c$.For acyclic quivers, the formula reduces to a permutation formula with coefficients depending only on descent numbers. We derive this formula independently from the quantum Magnus expansion using operator products and Wick contractions, showing that the physical graph coefficients are governed by the convolution structure of the contraction Hopf algebra. Further consequences include a refined quantum Murua formula and orientation-sum identities related to Tutte and chromatic polynomials.

hep-th.title: Semiclassical Cosmological Constant in Anti-de Sitter and de Sitter Spacetimes
hep-th.author: Milton C. Mamani-Leqque
hep-th.abstract: We investigate the semiclassical Einstein equation for a quantized scalar field in four-dimensional anti-de Sitter (AdS) and de Sitter (dS) spacetimes. We first determine self-consistent configurations by fixing the bare cosmological constant to its geometric value, requiring the renormalized vacuum stress-energy tensor to vanish. In AdS, the resulting mass-curvature relations depend on the curvature coupling and boundary conditions; one formal Neumann root for minimal coupling is excluded by the admissible parameter range, whereas both Dirichlet and Neumann solutions are allowed for conformal coupling. In dS, we recover the known self-consistent solution for a minimally coupled massive field. We then evaluate the effective cosmological constant on prescribed backgrounds in four massless configurations. In each case, it takes the form \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{eff}}=A/\ell^2+B/\ell^4\). The competition between classical curvature and vacuum polarization produces a minimum and a zero in the minimally coupled AdS case, while the other configurations are monotonic. Finally, the formal continuation \(\ell\rightarrow i\ell\) fails to reproduce the directly calculated quantum coefficients: their AdS-to-dS ratios are \(29/61\) for minimal coupling and \(-1\) for conformal coupling. These results show that continuation of the curvature scale alone does not establish equivalence between the semiclassical vacuum contributions in AdS and dS.
